Side Part
SYD PART
noun (Millennial slang)
A hairstyle in which the hair is divided on one side of the head rather than in the middle. Side parts were the default for decades, and the side-swept fringe was a 2000s emo and pop staple. In early 2021, in a viral TikTok exchange, Gen Z users declared the side part (along with skinny jeans and the laughing-crying emoji) a marker of Millennial "cringe," favouring the middle part; Millennials responded defensively, and the "side part debate" briefly became news.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

A side part is hair parted to one side, and in 2021 it became, absurdly, a generational badge: Gen Z declared it hopelessly Millennial, and Millennials defended it on TikTok as though something important were at stake. The Christian observation: the episode is mostly comedy, and comedy is a fine thing. But it offers a small lesson in vanity and in generations. First, vanity: people care intensely about how their hair falls, and Scripture gently reminds us that God cares about our hair more tenderly than we do: "But the very hairs of your head are all numbered" (Mat 10:30). The One who numbers them is not keeping score on the part. Peter tells believers not to make "plaiting the hair" their adorning, but the hidden man of the heart (1Pe 3:3-4). Second, generations: the side-part war was one generation mocking another over trivia, and it is a small picture of a larger pattern, each generation sneering at the last. Scripture asks for something better: "One generation shall praise thy works to another" (Psa 145:4). The old are to teach the young, and the young are to honour the old: "The glory of young men is their strength: and the beauty of old men is the gray head" (Pro 20:29). A father can laugh at the side-part war, part his hair however he likes, and teach his children that the hair on their heads is numbered by a loving Father, and that the best thing generations can trade is not mockery but praise of God.

Webster 1828 Definition

Millennial hairstyle mocked by Gen Z on TikTok (2021) as generational cringe; a comic episode with a small lesson: the hairs of your head are numbered (Mat 10:30), and generations should praise God to one another, not mock each other (Psa 145:4).

Decode for parents: a good-humoured chance to teach that generations should honour, not mock, each other.

Key Scripture

Mat 10:30 — "But the very hairs of your head are all numbered."

1Pe 3:3 — "Whose adorning let it not be that outward adorning of plaiting the hair, and of wearing of gold, or of putting on of apparel;"

Psa 145:4 — "One generation shall praise thy works to another, and shall declare thy mighty acts."

Pro 20:29 — "The glory of young men is their strength: and the beauty of old men is the gray head."

Pro 16:31 — "The hoary head is a crown of glory, if it be found in the way of righteousness."

Modern Corruption

The side part is a harmless hairstyle; the debate around it shows small vanity and generational mockery, which Scripture answers with numbered hairs and generations praising God together.

expand to see more

The only corruption here is the pettiness the debate exposed. Grown adults felt their identity threatened by a hair part, and teenagers built a sense of superiority on it. That is vanity on both sides, and it is the generational contempt that runs through modern culture in larger matters too: the young despising the old, the old dismissing the young. Scripture builds the opposite: "The hoary head is a crown of glory, if it be found in the way of righteousness" (Pro 16:31).

The redemption is humour and honour. Christians can laugh at hair debates, part their hair however they like, and refuse to mock anyone for it. And they can use the moment to teach the young to honour the old and the old to bless the young, so that one generation praises God’s works to another, which is a far better exchange than a TikTok war.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Latin pars (a portion) → part (a division, including of the hair) → side part → 2021 TikTok generational debate.
